svg.aria-label: What wsl-shrinker reads and what it changes. It reads WSL's own answers (the distributions Windows lists, which run, WSL's version), the disk files (the VHDX block table and its log, ext4's block bitmaps) and, inside a running distribution, the sizes of caches and images. It runs as you, with no administrator rights and no network. It changes a disk only through Windows, with wsl --manage --compact or the virtual disk API; inside a distribution only the items you chose, and the containers it stops and starts again; its own files: the settings, the history and the run's journal; and when you uninstall it, the program and its entry in your PATH. Nothing changes before you confirm a shrink or an uninstall, and a protected disk is never shrunk.
